issues.title: Checkout total is a cent too high for some orders
issues.author: support-team
issues.body:
Customers keep telling us our totals are one cent higher than the receipt from the till.

## Example
A blue pen, a red pen and a black pen, $0.10 each (all taxable). Checkout shows tax of **$0.03**, but 8.25% of $0.30 is $0.02475, which is $0.02.

Another one: a mug ($8.00) plus the same three pens. We charge $0.69 tax; the till charges $0.68.

## What I think is wrong
I'm pretty sure `Money.percent` rounds the wrong way. It should round down, not up.

## Expected
Tax on an order should be 8.25% of the order's taxable amount, rounded to the nearest cent.

issues.title: Coupons: the same code works twice, and lowercase codes are rejected
issues.author: qa-bot
issues.body:
Two problems with coupon codes.

1. Entering `SAVE10` twice gives 20% off instead of 10%.
2. Entering `save10`, or ` SAVE10` with a space pasted in front, fails at checkout with `UnknownCoupon`.

## Expected
- Codes are not case-sensitive and ignore spaces around them.
- Entering a code that is already on the cart does nothing.
- Different codes still stack (SAVE10 + WELCOME5 = 15% off), and codes that don't exist are still refused.

issues.title: Buy 2, get 1 free gives the wrong item away
issues.author: store-manager
issues.body:
A customer bought one pair of red socks ($6) and two pairs of wool socks ($15). The promotion took $15 off, but it should have been $6.

From the promotion terms: *if a cart has N items from the promotion, the N / 3 (rounded down) cheapest of them are free.* It shouldn't matter what order things were added to the cart in.

comments.author: store-manager
comments.body: Also seen with six pairs: we gave away a $15 pair and a $6 pair instead of two $6 pairs.
